news.title: Collins' Husband And Adviser Worked For Lobbyists Behind Data Center Push
news.description: Maine Sen. Susan Collins’ husband did consulting work for Chesapeake Enterprises, a lobbying firm that has pushed for more data center development. This was in 2025 when the firm’s only registered lobbyist was Scott Reed, the man at the center of an alleged pay-to-play scheme that is now threatening to derail Collins’ reelection campaign. Concerns about data centers and political corruption have consistently ranked as top issues for voters this year. Now, Collins is playing defense on both matters simultaneously. Collins married Thomas Daffron in 2012. Daffron had worked as a lobbyist, business consultant, and Republican political advisor. Collins’ net worth went from $250,000 to $2.9 million when they tied the knot. Today, it’s up to $4.1 million. Collins’ personal financial disclosures filed in May indicate that Daffron was paid at least $1,000 in consulting fees last year by Chesapeake Enterprises. Senate rules require spouses to report any income exceeding $1,000, but not the exact amount. Daffron previously served as the firm’s executive vice president from 2001 to 2004. Daffron was advising Chesapeake Enterprises when they lobbied the federal government last year on behalf of Hillwood Investments, a real estate development company that is chaired by billionaire H. Ross Perot Jr., a Collins campaign donor . Hillwood Investments helped build at least six data centers now operating in the U.S., including a Texas facility run by Meta, the parent company of Facebook. These centers, which provide the computing power needed to train and run AI systems, have become controversial for their excessive use of electricity and water, which has contributed to rising utility bills across the country. A recent New York Times /Siena poll found that 61 percent of Americans oppose building data centers in their communities. Multiple communities in Maine have now enacted moratoriums on building more data centers. Reed was Chesapeake Enterprises’s registered lobbyist for the Hillwood Investments account in 2025. Disclosures indicate that Reed lobbied the House and Senate on topics related to “real estate investments.” Reed is also the head of Pine Tree Results, a super PAC supporting Collins. In 2019, the FBI investigated Reed over a large donation he solicited from Navatek, a defense contractor. Former Navatek CEO Martin Kao, who is currently serving a prison sentence for wire fraud, told investigators that he gave the donation with the understanding that Collins would then help his company secure millions of dollars worth of federal contracts, which she ultimately did. The FBI investigation into Reed was dropped shortly after President Donald Trump returned to the White House. The alleged scheme was first reported by ProPublica on September 22. Collins has questioned the legitimacy of the report and steadfastly denied that any scheme existed. She has also publicly defended Reed. ProPublica has stood by its story and pushed back on Collins’ denials. Collins voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act, a bill that would theoretically require large data centers to cover their own electricity costs rather than passing them onto consumers. Senate Democrats say the legislation is toothless, noting that while it requires state public utility commissions to hold hearings and consider standards for data center cost-sharing, it is not mandatory that those standards actually be enacted. “It’s just fakery to try to fool voters into forgetting that Republicans spent the entire term trying to stop states from regulating AI,” Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy told Yahoo Finance . The Ratepayer Protection Act failed to pass the Senate on September 30. Collins is seeking a sixth term this year and is widely regarded as one of the most vulnerable Republican incumbents facing reelection. Her Democratic opponent, state Sen. Troy Jackson, says data center development should only be greenlit if it has a measurable benefit for Mainers. Reprinted with permission from American Journal News

news.title: IT’S (D)IFFERENT: ABC Selectively Reports Senate Candidate Gaffes
news.description: IT’S (D)IFFERENT: ABC Selectively Reports Senate Candidate Gaffes Color us shocked: it appears that the Disney-owned American Broadcasting Company, with its status as a purveyor of bona fide news programming currently in dispute , is selective about which perceived candidate misstatements or gaffes make it to air. Take one guess as to what that selection criteria is. ABC World News Tonight ended its A-block by hyping Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton’s quote questioning the effectiveness of the GOP midterm convention. Watch below: WATCH: @ABCWorldNews is selective about which Senate candidate faux pas to cover. Pouncing on "Republicans in Disarray" and "POLLS DOOM!1!" angle for Ken Paxton's critique of the midterm convention, absolute zero on Troy Jackson's awful Holocaust quote, to wit: "It’s unfortunate… pic.twitter.com/tMqn3mje1z — Jorge Bonilla (@BonillaJL) October 1, 2026 ABC WORLD NEWS TONIGHT 9/30/26 6:45 PM DAVID MUIR: Now to the midterm elections tonight, just weeks away, now. This evening, the Texas Senate race and what the Republican in that race is caught on audio saying about President Trump and the president's recent convention in Texas. Here's Mary Bruce tonight. MARY BRUCE: Tonight, in audio obtained by the New York Times, Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate in the closely watched Texas Senate race, can be heard complaining President Trump's recent midterm convention in Dallas hurt Republican campaigns, including his own. KEN PAXTON: When we did that convention- it dropped our numbers. Everybody's numbers dropped. Right now, yeah. Not good. BRUCE: In a remarkable leadup to the midterms, polls in the reliably red state now give Paxton's Democratic opponent, James Talarico, a slight edge. Paxton, the Texas attorney general, has weathered personal scandals and corruption allegations. Talarico, a former middle school teacher and student minister, making inroads into even some of the reddest parts of the state. During the Republican midterm convention, Talarico held a food drive nearby. JAMES TALARICO: They are toasting to their own corruption. BRUCE: Late today, the president asked about Paxton's comments, blaming Trump's convention for his campaign woes. DONALD TRUMP: Well, I haven't heard that, but I can tell you that the convention was amazing. BRUCE: But polls put his approval rating at or near record lows, in some cases as bad as in the aftermath of January 6th. And tonight, Texas’s outgoing Republican Senator, John Cornyn, with a warning. JOHN CORNYN: The president wants to make all these elections about himself when his favorability ratings are not what they once were. That's not a plus. That's a negative. MUIR: And, Mary, we should point out that despite that audio capture, President Trump is scheduled to be in Texas tomorrow to campaign with Ken Paxton. I know you're going to track that. In the meantime, while we have you tonight, the other major headline. This involves changes at the Pentagon and a shift for the U.S. in Iraq? BRUCE: And David, in the middle of this war with Iran, Secretary Pete Hegseth today announcing he is slashing the number of generals and admirals at the Pentagon by 20%. It comes on the same day that U.S. forces have now formally withdrawn from Iraq after more than two decades. MUIR: Mary Bruce at The White House tonight. Mary, thank you. For ABC, this is a no-brainer. They get to do “Republicans in Disarray” AND run another “Polling DOOM” story in which no actual polls are cited. For their “Republicans in Disarray” angle they got a quote from outgoing Texas Senator John Cornyn. Were the shoe on the other party’s foot, you’d never hear a quote from a primary-losing Democrat. In fact, when’s the last time any of these networks got a quote from Jasmine Crockett on James Talarico? ABC managed to sneak THIS story in at the end of their A-block but there was another story they could’ve done, with a more damaging quote from the Senate candidate. THAT candidate, though, is a Democrat. And not just a Democrat, but the Democrat that was selected to replace Nazi-adjacent Graham “Herr Totenkopf” Platner in Maine. Per NBC News Center Maine : Maine Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson is apologizing for comments he made this week in a NEWS CENTER Maine candidate profile interview about Israeli “genocide” in Gaza. In reiterating his view that that the three-year-old Israel-Gaza war “is a genocide,” Jackson said in the interview, “There are people here in Maine that don't like to use that term only because, you know, they're Jewish and, you know, what that means to them with the Holocaust.” Imagine the media reaction had a Republican said such a thing about the Holocaust. The dudgeon would be through the roof, if for no other reason than to deflect from the left’s very real antisemitism problem. You’d have at least a weeklong cycle atop A-block on both network news and cable. ABC displays a blatant double standard here by running the Paxton story while omitting Jackson. As we often say: if it weren’t for double standards there would be none at all.
